result:alice-hypertriton-lifetime-2019.name: (Anti-)hypertriton lifetime measurement in Pb-Pb collisions at 5.02 TeV

summary.plain: ALICE measured how long a rare, fragile nucleus called the hypertriton survives before decaying, using lead-lead collisions at the LHC, helping settle a long-running disagreement between earlier experiments' measurements.

result:alice-hypertriton-lifetime-2019.title: 3_Lambda H and 3_Lambdabar Hbar lifetime measurement in Pb-Pb collisions at sqrt(s_NN) = 5.02 TeV via two-body decay

result:alice-jpsi-suppression-pbpb-2012.name: J/psi suppression at forward rapidity in Pb-Pb collisions at 2.76 TeV

summary.plain: ALICE measured how often J/psi particles (made of a charm quark and antiquark) survive lead-lead collisions at the LHC, finding less suppression than expected from lower-energy experiments, consistent with new J/psi particles re-forming inside the hot quark-gluon plasma.

result:alice-jpsi-suppression-pbpb-2012.title: J/psi suppression at forward rapidity in Pb-Pb collisions at sqrt(s_NN) = 2.76 TeV

summary.plain: ALICE found that, in the busiest ordinary proton-proton collisions, unusual 'strange' particles are produced far more often than normal - a pattern previously seen only in collisions of heavy atomic nuclei and linked to the quark-gluon plasma.

result:alice-strangeness-enhancement-pp-.title: Enhanced production of multi-strange hadrons in high-multiplicity proton-proton collisions

result:atlas-hbb-observation-2018.name: Observation of the Higgs boson decay to bottom quarks

summary.plain: ATLAS saw the Higgs boson decaying into bottom quarks - its single most common decay - by looking for it alongside a W or Z boson.

result:atlas-hbb-observation-2018.title: Observation of H -> bbbar decays and VH production with the ATLAS detector

result:atlas-higgs-observation-2012.name: Observation of a new particle in the search for the Standard Model Higgs boson

summary.plain: On 4 July 2012, ATLAS announced it had found a new particle weighing about 126 times as much as a proton. The collaboration was careful to call it 'a new particle', not yet 'the Higgs boson' - that identification came with later data.

result:atlas-higgs-observation-2012.title: Observation of a new particle in the search for the Standard Model Higgs boson with the ATLAS detector at the LHC

result:atlas-htautau-observation-2018.key_value_text: Observation of H -> tau tau decays, 6.4 sigma observed significance
result:atlas-htautau-observation-2018.name: Observation of the Higgs boson decay to a pair of tau leptons

summary.plain: ATLAS saw, on its own, the Higgs boson decaying into a pair of tau leptons - heavy cousins of the electron - confirming that the Higgs couples to this type of particle.

result:atlas-htautau-observation-2018.title: Cross-section measurements of the Higgs boson decaying into a pair of tau-leptons in proton-proton collisions at sqrt(s)=13 TeV with the ATLAS detector

result:atlas-lbyl-observation-2019.name: Observation of light-by-light scattering in lead-lead collisions

summary.plain: ATLAS watched two particles of light bounce off each other - a process so rare it needs the electromagnetic fields of whole lead nuclei grazing past one another to see it at all.

result:atlas-lbyl-observation-2019.title: Observation of light-by-light scattering in ultraperipheral Pb+Pb collisions with the ATLAS detector

result:atlas-nature-higgs-2022.name: A detailed map of Higgs boson interactions, ten years after the discovery

summary.plain: Ten years after finding it, ATLAS put together everything it had learned about the Higgs boson: how it is made, how it decays, and how closely all of that matches the theory. Everything still fits.

result:atlas-nature-higgs-2022.title: A detailed map of Higgs boson interactions by the ATLAS experiment ten years after the discovery

result:atlas-squark-gluino-limit-2020.name: Exclusion limits on squarks and gluinos from the full Run 2 dataset

summary.plain: ATLAS searched its full second run of LHC data for supersymmetric partner particles called squarks and gluinos, found no sign of them, and used that to rule out gluinos lighter than about 2.3 trillion electronvolts under a simple model.

result:atlas-squark-gluino-limit-2020.title: Search for squarks and gluinos in final states with jets and missing transverse momentum using 139 fb^-1 of sqrt(s)=13 TeV pp collision data with the ATLAS detector

result:atlas-topmass-measurement-2018.name: Measurement of the top quark mass

summary.plain: ATLAS weighed the top quark, the heaviest known elementary particle, using 8 TeV collision data and combined the result with its earlier measurements.

result:atlas-topmass-measurement-2018.title: Measurement of the top quark mass in the ttbar -> lepton+jets channel from sqrt(s)=8 TeV ATLAS data and combination with previous results

result:atlas-tth-observation-2018.name: Observation of Higgs boson production in association with a top quark pair

summary.plain: ATLAS observed Higgs bosons being made together with a top quark and its antiparticle, the most direct way to see how strongly the Higgs sticks to the heaviest known particle.

result:atlas-tth-observation-2018.title: Observation of Higgs boson production in association with a top quark pair at the LHC with the ATLAS detector

result:atlas-wmass-measurement-2017.name: Measurement of the W boson mass

summary.plain: ATLAS weighed the W boson, a carrier of the weak force, using 7 TeV collision data - one of the most precise measurements of this mass from any single experiment at the time.

result:atlas-wmass-measurement-2017.title: Measurement of the W-boson mass in pp collisions at sqrt(s)=7 TeV with the ATLAS detector

result:belle-b-to-tau-nu-evidence-2006.name: Evidence for the purely leptonic decay B⁻ → τ⁻ ν̅

summary.plain: Belle found the first evidence that a B particle can decay straight into a tau lepton and a neutrino. Because the neutrino is invisible, the decay had to be inferred from everything else in the event.

result:belle-b-to-tau-nu-evidence-2006.title: Evidence of the Purely Leptonic Decay B⁻ → τ⁻ ν̅_τ

result:belle-cp-violation-observation-20.name: Observation of large CP violation in the neutral B meson system

summary.plain: Belle showed that neutral B particles and their antiparticles decay at measurably different rates — the first clear sign of this matter–antimatter asymmetry outside the kaon system. It confirmed the Kobayashi–Maskawa explanation of CP violation, recognised with the 2008 Nobel Prize in Physics.

result:belle-cp-violation-observation-20.title: Observation of Large CP Violation in the Neutral B Meson System

summary.plain: Belle found evidence that a neutral D particle can turn into its own antiparticle before it decays — a very slow effect that had been searched for since the 1970s.

result:belle-ii-b-to-k-nunu-evidence-202.name: Evidence for B⁺ → K⁺ νν̅ decays

summary.plain: Belle II saw the first evidence for a very rare B decay into a kaon and two neutrinos. Because the neutrinos leave no trace, the decay is found by showing that nothing else in the event accounts for the missing energy. The measured rate is somewhat higher than the Standard Model predicts.

result:belle-ii-b-to-k-nunu-evidence-202.title: Evidence for B⁺ → K⁺ ν ν̅ decays

result:belle-ii-tau-mass-measurement-202.name: Measurement of the τ-lepton mass

summary.plain: Belle II made the most precise measurement yet of the mass of the tau, the heaviest of the three charged leptons. The mass is a fundamental constant of nature that the Standard Model does not predict.

result:belle-ii-tau-mass-measurement-202.title: Measurement of the τ-lepton mass with the Belle II experiment

result:belle-ii-vcb-measurement-2025.name: Determination of |Vcb| using B→Dℓνℓ Decays at Belle II

summary.plain: Belle II measured how often a B meson (a particle containing a bottom quark) decays into a D meson plus a lepton and neutrino, and used that to pin down |Vcb|, a fundamental number that sets how strongly bottom and charm quarks convert into each other.

result:belle-ii-vcb-measurement-2025.title: Determination of |Vcb| using B→Dℓνℓ Decays at Belle II

result:belle-x3872-observation-2003.name: Observation of the X(3872)

summary.plain: Belle spotted an unexpected new particle, later called the X(3872), that does not fit the simple picture of a quark and an antiquark orbiting each other. It opened the study of 'exotic' hadrons, and dozens more have been found since.

result:belle-x3872-observation-2003.title: Observation of a narrow charmonium-like state in exclusive B± → K± π⁺π⁻ J/ψ decays

result:borexino-cno-evidence-2020.key_value_text: Excess of a few counts per day per 100 t of target attributed to CNO-neutrino interactions

result:borexino-cno-evidence-2020.title: Experimental evidence of neutrinos produced in the CNO fusion cycle in the Sun

result:borexino-pp-first-detection-2014.name: Neutrinos from the primary proton–proton fusion process in the Sun

summary.plain: Borexino directly measured, for the first time, the spectrum of the most common neutrinos the Sun makes — the ones from the very first step of the reaction that powers it.

result:borexino-pp-first-detection-2014.title: Neutrinos from the primary proton–proton fusion process in the Sun

result:cdf-top-quark-observation-1995.name: Observation of Top Quark Production in ppbar Collisions with the Collider Detector at Fermilab

result:cdf-top-quark-observation-1995.title: Observation of Top Quark Production in ppbar Collisions with the Collider Detector at Fermilab

result:cms-higgs-boson-observation-2012.name: Observation of a new boson at a mass of 125 GeV

summary.plain: CMS found a new particle weighing about 125 times as much as a proton, the last missing piece of the standard model of particle physics. ATLAS announced the same discovery on the same day.

result:cms-higgs-boson-observation-2012.title: Observation of a new boson at a mass of 125 GeV with the CMS experiment at the LHC

result:cms-higgs-boson-portrait-2022.name: A portrait of the Higgs boson ten years after the discovery

summary.plain: Ten years after the discovery, CMS put together everything it had learned about the Higgs boson: how it is made, how it decays, its mass and its spin - all so far matching the theory.

result:cms-higgs-boson-portrait-2022.title: A portrait of the Higgs boson by the CMS experiment ten years after the discovery

result:cms-higgs-to-bb-observation-2018.name: Observation of Higgs boson decay to bottom quarks

summary.plain: CMS saw the Higgs boson decaying into bottom quarks, which is what it does most of the time but is very hard to pick out from the flood of ordinary collisions.

result:cms-higgs-to-bb-observation-2018.title: Observation of Higgs boson decay to bottom quarks

result:cms-higgs-to-tau-tau-observation-.name: Observation of the Higgs boson decay to tau leptons

result:cms-higgs-to-tau-tau-observation-.title: Observation of the Higgs boson decay to a pair of tau leptons with the CMS detector

result:cms-high-mass-dilepton-search-202.name: Most stringent limits on new high-mass dilepton resonances

summary.plain: CMS looked through its whole Run 2 dataset for pairs of electrons or muons from a heavy new particle, found nothing, and so ruled out a wide range of proposed new particles.

result:cms-high-mass-dilepton-search-202.title: Search for resonant and nonresonant new phenomena in high-mass dilepton final states at sqrt(s) = 13 TeV

result:cms-lhcb-bs-to-mumu-observation-2.name: Observation of the rare decay Bs0 -> mu+ mu- (CMS and LHCb combined)

result:cms-lhcb-bs-to-mumu-observation-2.title: Observation of the rare $B^0_s\to\mu^+\mu^-$ decay from the combined analysis of CMS and LHCb data

result:cms-long-range-near-side-correlat.name: Observation of long-range near-side angular correlations in pp collisions ("the ridge")

summary.plain: In its first year CMS saw pairs of particles flying in the same direction but far apart along the beam, a pattern nobody expected in ordinary proton collisions and previously seen only in collisions of heavy nuclei.

result:cms-long-range-near-side-correlat.title: Observation of Long-Range Near-Side Angular Correlations in Proton-Proton Collisions at the LHC

result:cms-top-quark-mass-measurement-20.name: Top quark mass measured to 0.37 GeV

result:cms-top-quark-mass-measurement-20.title: Measurement of the top quark mass using a profile likelihood approach with the lepton+jets final states in proton-proton collisions at sqrt(s) = 13 TeV

summary.plain: CMS measured the mass of the W boson more precisely than any other LHC experiment, and found it to agree with the standard model - unlike an earlier, conflicting result from the Tevatron.

result:cms-w-boson-mass-measurement-2024.title: High-precision measurement of the W boson mass with the CMS experiment

result:coherent-argon-measurement-2021.name: First Measurement of Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering on Argon

result:xenon1t-electronic-recoil-excess-.key_value_text: Excess most prominent between 2 and 3 keV; if interpreted as a monoenergetic peak, centered at (2.3+-0.2) keV with 3.0 sigma global (4.0 sigma local) significance -- interpretation unconfirmed.
result:xenon1t-electronic-recoil-excess-.name: Excess Electronic Recoil Events in XENON1T
result:xenon1t-electronic-recoil-excess-.significance: up to 3.4 sigma (solar axion hypothesis, before tritium is allowed to float; reduces to 2.0 sigma if an unconstrained tritium component is included)

summary.plain: In 2020, XENON1T reported seeing more low-energy electron-recoil events than expected. The excess was never confirmed as dark matter, a new particle or any other specific cause -- possible explanations included a tiny amount of natural radioactivity (tritium) in the detector, solar particles called axions, or a new neutrino property -- and it remains an open, unresolved anomaly.

result:xenon1t-electronic-recoil-excess-.title: Excess Electronic Recoil Events in XENON1T

result:xenonnt-b8-cevns-indication-2024.key_value_text: Measured 8B solar-neutrino flux of (4.7+3.6-2.3)e6 cm^-2 s^-1, consistent with prior measurements (e.g. SNO).
result:xenonnt-b8-cevns-indication-2024.name: First Indication of Solar 8B Neutrinos via Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering with XENONnT

summary.plain: XENONnT saw a hint -- not yet a firm discovery -- of solar neutrinos bouncing gently off xenon nuclei, a process too faint for most detectors to see. The signal is weak (under 3-sigma), but if confirmed it would make XENONnT one of the smallest neutrino detectors in the world.

result:xenonnt-b8-cevns-indication-2024.title: First Indication of Solar 8B Neutrinos via Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering with XENONnT

result:xenonnt-first-nr-search-2023.name: First Dark Matter Search with Nuclear Recoils from the XENONnT Experiment

summary.plain: XENONnT looked for dark matter particles bumping into xenon nuclei for the first time. It saw nothing beyond ordinary background, which let it rule out a wide range of possible dark matter particles more tightly than any liquid-xenon experiment before it.

result:xenonnt-first-nr-search-2023.title: First Dark Matter Search with Nuclear Recoils from the XENONnT Experiment
